dedupe_keys.name: standardised protocol for pre and post storm urban forest data collection

description: This article sets out a standardised protocol for collecting data on urban forests before and after storms, drawn from earlier studies and the authors' experience gathering urban tree data after severe storms. The authors note that there is often little time to set up sampling before clean-up removes evidence of failure modes and damage severity, and that storms vary in frequency, so researchers may lack practice in storm assessment. The protocol covers tree species, size and condition, risk factors and damage type, and gives instructions for post-storm collection by field survey, remote sensing and citizen science, aligned with what urban forest managers already record. Coverage: generic, written for hurricanes, ice storms and tornadoes. Access: article on the journal site. Licence: not stated on the page read. Caveats: a protocol, not a dataset; it standardises attributes that future inventories and damage surveys should share. Simulation uses: building consistent tree inventories and damage records to fit street-tree wind fragility curves and model tree-fall impacts on roads and power lines. Related records: the Tongji street-tree wind fragility model, the NYC street tree census and London public realm trees.
